summary: Before ERCOT begins an interconnection study, the draft rule would require the customer to execute an intermediate agreement with the transmission provider including demonstration of site control through a deed, purchase option or lease, and disclosure of duplicate service requests.

source.citation: Law firm client publications on the draft rule, March 2026

notes: Duplicate-service-request disclosure addresses queue inflation directly: a single project applying at multiple interconnection points is the mechanism that makes published pipeline figures unreadable. If adopted as drafted, this would be the first requirement identified anywhere that a developer state on the record whether it has applied elsewhere for the same load. Site control by deed or option is separately a county recorder record.
confidence_note: Draft rule not read. Whether the provision survives adoption is NOT_CHECKED, and whether any disclosure becomes public or stays with the transmission provider is unestablished.
